parsed.explanation: Strong traveler-facing positives: constitutional SOGI protection, self-ID recognition (2016, streamlined 2024), same-sex marriage, conversion practices criminalized as torture, pride marches with police protection and official participation, rainbow-lit monuments, a penalized hostile politician, and trans elected officials — documented social acceptance that outvotes the 2011 conservative snapshot. The dominant exposure is custody: an almost universally male prison system places trans women (including a detained foreign national, 2023) in male pavilions with documented sexual violence, beatings, and deaths in custody (2021, 2026), and the protective pavilion operates unevenly — a tier-1 state practice with no shown remedy. This is conditional on detention, not universal, so it does not anchor the score lower. Rising general violence amid armed conflict is largely out of scope absent trans-specific targeting with denominators. Net: acceptance with an unremedied carceral exposure.
